newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia's Nemtsov details state role in Gazprom.
newsitem.headline: Russia's Nemtsov details state role in Gazprom.

text.p: The Russian government and natural gas monopoly Gazprom have agreed a number of measures increasing the government role in company management, First Deputy Prime Minister Boris Nemtsov said on Tuesday.

Nemtsov, who is in charge of a campaign to revamp natural monopolies -- large companies with no competitors such as the railways -- said Gazprom and the government had a "completely partner-like relationship", Prime-Tass news agency said.

Nemtsov said the role of the government, acting through a representative to the company, should increase transparency, regulate tariffs and ensure equal access to gas fields and pipelines for all firms wishing to work in the sector.
He also said the government's aim should be to facilitate regular tax payments and promote higher prices for shares in RAO Gazprom, the world's largest natural gas producer.

Nemtsov said an agreement was being worked out to govern how the government's 35 percent share in Gazprom 0#GAZP.RUO will be held in trust in the future. It is now managed by Gazprom chairman Rem Vyakhirev.
Deputy Prime Minister Alfred Kokh, who is also privatisation minister, recently said the government should consider what he called Vyakhirev's personal control of the stake.

Tass quoted Nemtsov as saying that, under the new agreement, it would not matter who happened to be the head of Gazprom since the shares would be transferred to another holder if the trust agreement rules were broken.
The government renewed Vyakhirev's control of the stake, originally granted in 1993, last year, Kokh said.
